item.title: Policy and Public Affairs Manager
item.description: Internet Matters is a not-for-profit committed to keeping children safe online. We are one of the leading online safety organisations in the UK, working with major global brands including founding members BT/EE, Sky and Virgin Media O2 as well as partners such as TikTok, Samsung and Roblox. We’re here to offer the best advice and information available to help parents, carers and professionals engage in the online lives of children and young people, empowering them to manage the risks they may face online. We conduct regular research on families’ online experiences and use these insights to influence policymakers, regulators and government, helping to drive positive outcomes for children’s online safety and media literacy. About the role It is an exciting time to be working in children’s online safety. New measures restricting popular social media platforms’ access to children, alongside existing requirements under the Online Safety Act, are reshaping the role of technology companies in keeping children safe online. At the same time, curriculum reform, votes at 16 and the Government’s mission to halve violence against women and girls (VAWG) create real opportunities to shape online safety and media literacy policy, and improve outcomes for children and young people. Yet the challenges families face online are evolving at pace, from mis- and disinformation to the rapid adoption of AI. There is cross-party consensus on the importance of tackling these issues, and now is the moment to harness this momentum to drive lasting change for children. Against this backdrop, Internet Matters is recruiting a Policy and Public Affairs Manager to help ensure online safety policy works in practice and improves outcomes for families. This wide-ranging role will include: Stakeholder engagement, public affairs and influencing, including maintaining and developing a network of contacts across Government, Parliament, regulators, civil society and industry. Identifying opportunities to push forward our agenda with decision-makers, including through convening meetings and events and actively contributing to events held by others. Supporting the development of Internet Matters’ policy positions, ensuring they are underpinned by the latest research and informed by the sector and political landscape. Key policy areas the role will lead on are media literacy, safeguarding girls online and supporting children with SEND online. Monitoring UK parliamentary business and proactively finding opportunities to influence. Writing policy outputs for a range of audiences including social copy, blogs, briefings, reports and responses to consultations and calls for evidence. Presenting and sharing policy and research in a range of settings, including at external meetings and events, tailoring messages to different audiences. Acting as secretariat for Internet Matters’ Vulnerable User Working Group and Expert Advisory Panel. Contributing your ideas to team discussions about the overarching strategy for our policy and research work. This role sits within the Policy and Research team and a core aspect of the role will be the ability to shape research and insights for policy and sector audiences. You will also support with the analysis of research in relation to policy related tasks. About you The successful candidate will have professional experience of working in policy, public affairs or a closely related field. They may have gained this experience from another charity/not-for-profit, a regulator, government, parliament or industry. Although not required, experience of one of the following sector or policy areas would be an advantage: tech, online safety, education, tech-facilitated VAWG or SEND. We are particularly keen to hear from candidates that have experience writing outputs for a range of audiences and translating primary research into engaging policy insights. You will also have experience building and maintaining relationships with sector, policy and parliamentary stakeholders. The ideal candidate will have a strong eye for detail and take pride in producing high-quality work. We are seeking someone excited by the opportunity of working in a small organisation, where everyone lends a hand to deliver key priorities, and where you can contribute actively to our wider thinking and strategy. Supporting Documents The documents below relate to the job you are applying for, click on any of the links to download and view: To Apply Please click on the Apply button below to email your submit a cover letter setting out how you meet the skills, knowledge and experience criteria, along with your CV. When you submit your application, please can you also provide the following information: Please state clearly that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network; Your current notice period (if applicable); Confirmation that you have legal authorisation to work in the UK. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Tuesday 29th September 2026

item.title: Researcher
item.description: Henham Strategy is looking for talented, enthusiastic people early in their careers in public affairs and policy to join us as a Researcher in our London-based team. Henham Strategy is a policy and public affairs consultancy. We combine rigorous research, strategic insights, unrivalled connections, and decades of experience to focus on delivering client outcomes. With our broad range of government, industry and political backgrounds, we have an exceptional track record of supporting public sector organisations, trade bodies, charities and the private sector. Our hard-working team is driven by an unwavering commitment to our clients and a desire to unlock compelling opportunities for those we work with. ‍What we’re looking for The ideal candidate is someone who wants to use their passion for UK policy and politics in a fast-paced, business environment. We are looking for enthusiastic and motivated individuals with curiosity about the world and a hunger to learn, with strong written and verbal communication skills and a desire to grow their networks. In supporting the team as we deliver high quality work for our clients, we are looking for people who are organised, diligent and have good attention to detail. The successful candidate would ideally have some experience in policy or politics. ‍Responsibilities Researchers are responsible for leading research on political and policy-related issues on behalf of our client base. The role is varied but typical tasks include: Developing briefing and stakeholder mapping material; Compiling accurate monitoring reports for clients; Carrying out both qualitative and quantitative research and policy analysis on a variety of different topics; Supporting with organising client events such as Parliamentary receptions; Attending relevant meetings and events on behalf of clients; Starting to establish business and political networks; Monitoring media, news and updates on a variety of client portfolios. ‍Benefits Company-wide benefits include: Private health insurance cover; including GP service, mental health support, and dental and optical cover 25 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays with the option to carry over 5 days per year. Hybrid working, with a minimum of three days a week in our London office 'Work from Away': up to 5 days a year, including from locations outside the UK Annual discretionary bonus, subject to company and individual performance • Pension: employer contributions matched up to 5% To Apply Please click on the Apply button below for more information, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Applications will close at noon on Monday the 28th of September. Initial phone screenings will take place in the w/c 28th of September. First round of virtual interviews will be in the w/c 5th of October. Final in-person interview will be in the w/c 12th of October in our London office. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 12:00pm on Monday 28th September 2026
